description: We are That日本, building a human-centered health monitoring dashboard for astronauts on long-duration space missions. Our goal is to simplify vital telemetry, track real-time biometric trends, and reduce crew cognitive load in microgravity.
summary:
That日本 is a 100% offline-first Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) and zero-gravity cockpit dashboard engineered for Earth-Independent Medical Operations (EIMO) on deep-space missions to the Moon and Mars. Because communication latency with Earth can reach 5 to 20 minutes each way, astronauts cannot rely on real-time ground flight surgeons during medical emergencies or rapid physiological decline.

That日本 solves this by continuously processing crew biometric telemetry, environmental hazards, and cognitive fatigue metrics locally onboard without requiring an internet or ground server connection. Its core Multi-Stressor Cross-Correlation Matrix detects non-linear risk escalation when overlapping sub-threshold hazards—such as Solar Particle Event (SPE) radiation, elevated cabin CO₂, sleep deprivation, and microgravity cardiovascular deconditioning—compound simultaneously. Grounded in NASA-STD-3001 standards and NASA GeneLab multi-omics baselines, That日本 provides early-warning alerts, step-by-step clinical action checklists, Psychomotor Vigilance Testing (PVT), voice-assisted symptom logging, and circadian-adaptive UI modes to protect crew health and mission autonomy.
details:
What It Does & How It Works That日本 is an autonomous Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS), designed for high-latency deep space operations. This system works as a zero-gravity health console system providing crew bio-data such as Heart Rate, Heart Rate Variability, Total Radiation Exposure and Hours Slept, as well as ECLSS data (CO₂ levels etc.)

Multi-Stressor Correlation Matrix This calculates the overall risk based on multiple stresses the crew is exposed to whilst on their mission. This is done by looking at individual vital signs and correlating them to give an overall risk value, e.g. an increase in Solar Radiation, CO₂ levels and Sleep Deprivation.

Clinical Procedures This triggers interactive checklists for medical procedures to be performed when the sensor data goes above NASA-STD-3001 AMBER DEGRADED/RED CRITICAL limits.

Psychomotor Vigilance Task (PVT) This provides an interactive 3 trial PVT task which can calculate the reaction time and laps in ms.

Voice Input This allows astronauts to document symptoms using a voice recognition simulation.

Store & Forward This stores all medical events, alerts and results. It also stores encrypted data in a queue to be sent back to Mission Control once a connection is made.

Benefit & Impact With human spaceflight now moving into lunar (Artemis) and Martian missions, real-time telemedicine isn’t possible. That日本 helps provide autonomy to allow astronauts (who aren’t a medical professional) to identify small changes in multiple systems within the body. It also helps reduce the risk of acute radiation and fatigue issues. It helps ensure astronauts are always at optimal cognitive performance, without having to wait up to 40 minutes to get instructions from earth.

Tools & Technologies Used

Front End React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS

Visualisation Recharts (Multi Sol Analysis of Radiation, PVT/Sleep, Cardiovascular and ECLSS data.), Lucide React.

Architecture Multi agent system design using agent.yaml. Designed to be used offline to create clinical rules and follow NASA-STD-3001.

Creative Design

Circadian Theme This has an inbuilt Circadian theme system. This means that the theme will change depending on the time of day. During work times the theme will be a high contrast blue/cyan. During pre-sleep, the theme will be a red shift (Inspired by 650nm wavelength). During sleep the theme will be set to sleep mode.

Stressor Triggers This has inbuilt triggers to simulate stressors such as Solar Particle Event, Acute Crew Fatigue and Sensor Noise. This lets flight surgeons and judges see how the CDSS handles triage situations and how the risk increases.
